lastCompletedStory.title: Prove the three fail-closed legs of install.sh by execution

nextStoryContext: test/install-sh.test.ts's 'install.sh fail-closed legs (US-004, CAM-495)' describe block now covers all three absence conditions by real execution, replacing the narrower US-003 'checksum verification' block it superseded (same behavior, strengthened assertions -- no coverage was dropped). All three legs assert both exit!=0 AND readdirSync(installDir)===[] in the same test (never split across two assertions/tests), matching the story's explicit 'both conditions together' requirement. Hash-mismatch and checksums-unavailable legs reuse writeFakeCurl, widened with a new 'checksums-unavailable' behavior value (the SHA256SUMS.txt branch exits 22 instead of writing a manifest, while the asset-download branch is untouched and still serves normally -- confirms install.sh's existing `if ! curl ...; then ERROR; exit 1; fi` guard around the manifest download was already fail-closed pre-story, no install.sh change was needed for either of those two legs). The no-hash-tool leg is new infrastructure: buildPathWithoutHashTools() symlinks real host binaries (via `/usr/bin/which <tool>`, resolved through the test process's own ambient PATH) for every external tool install.sh's main body OR its `trap ... EXIT` handler calls -- uname/mktemp/chmod/grep/sed/awk/mkdir/cp/rm, plus xattr on darwin -- into a fresh curated tools-only tmpdir, deliberately omitting sha256sum/shasum; GOTCHA (found live, not hypothesized): the first attempt omitted `rm` and got exit 127 ('command not found') instead of install.sh's own diagnostic, because the EXIT trap (`trap 'rm -f "${TMP_BIN}" "${TMP_SUMS}"' EXIT`) fires unconditionally on every exit path and corrupts the observed exit code if it can't resolve -- audit trap bodies for external-tool deps with the same rigor as the main body. The leg's own fake curl (writeNoHashToolCurl) is pure bash builtins (no cut/dirname/basename/hash-tool dependency, unlike the shared writeFakeCurl shim), so it works correctly even inside the stripped PATH; it bakes a fixed 64-'a' placeholder digest + a computed assetNameForHost() into the served manifest -- freezing the digest is correct here (not a violation of the general US-003 'never freeze a digest' guidance) because the no-hash-tool failure fires at the command -v resolution step, strictly before any digest-comparison assertion reads that value. runInstallSh() gained an optional envOverrides param (backward compatible, existing 0-arg call sites unaffected) so the no-hash-tool leg can substitute its curated PATH while the script is still invoked through the absolute /bin/bash interpreter path (unchanged from the CAM-460 helper), so a stripped PATH can never make bash itself unresolvable. All 9 ACs verified individually (oracle greps for 'hash mismatch'/'checksums unavailable'/'no hash tool'/'command not found'/'readdirSync' all pass) plus the full spine: typecheck 0 errors, bun test 6001 pass/0 fail (test/install-sh.test.ts: 7 pass), bun run check:all exit 0 (no budget/ignore-list edits needed, install-sh.test.ts is not in scripts/file-size-budget.json's tracked set so no ceiling was hit). Only test/install-sh.test.ts changed; no vendor/ or templates/ touch, so embed-vendor:check (already part of the spine) needed no extra standalone run.
